messages:
maria_awssec: Heads up — product asked if we can standardize event namespace for customer-visible audit events. Current chaos: some events are `user.*`, some `actor.*`, some mixed. cc @derek_prod @sophia_eng

_derek_prod: +1. Customer contracts require stable names. We should avoid verbs in past tense. Prefer action noun pattern like `key.rotate` not `key.rotated`._

_sophia_eng: Suggest pattern: <resource>.<action>.<phase?> e.g._
```
kms.key.rotate.started
kms.key.rotate.succeeded
kms.key.rotate.failed
```
_Keeps things predictable for parsers._

_owen_sre: Big +1. Also: downstream SIEMs and alerting rules depend on names. Any rename needs deprecation + mapping layer (forward/backwards compatibility)._

_maria_awssec: Agreed. Security requirements: public audit events must include `actor.id`, `actor.type`, `resource.id`, `request_id`, `ip`, `timestamp`. For KMS ops add `kms.key_id` and `kms.fingerprint` (never raw key material)._

_luis_priv: For BYOK flows include `tenant_id` and `envelope_key_id`. We should also add `integrity_hash` field for BYOK metadata, not the key._

_sophia_eng: Proposal: maintain a versioned manifest `events_public.json` in the repo listing stable names + schema + retention policy. Add a `public: true` flag to internal event schema to mark customer-visible ones._

_derek_prod: Ownership: Eng-Security defines naming + required fields, Eng-Platform implements compatibility layer and preserves old names for 90d, Product signs external docs and customer notices._

_platform-bot: RFC reminder: please file an RFC before mass renames: https://go/repo/rfcs -> "event-nomenclature". CI will block breaking schema changes._

_deploy-bot: RFC created: ID 5234 - event-nomenclature (status: draft)_

_maria_awssec: Action items — Sophia: draft manifest by EOW; Owen: enumerate downstream consumers and alerting rules; Derek: coordinate Product sign-off and legal check for contract impact. I'll surface KMS/retention constraints to Privacy._

_sophia_eng: Will do. I'll post the draft link in this thread when ready. :thumbsup:
